title: Winter Light Cathedral
location: Aotea Square, 291-297 Queen Street, Auckland City Centre, Auckland, Auckland
description:
Wander through a glowing tunnel of light and feel the magic of winter come alive!
Step inside Winter Light Cathedral - a dazzling, walk-through experience made from tens of thousands of tiny LED lights. Inspired by the sweeping arches of grand church windows, this luminous tunnel invites you in for a moment of warmth, wonder and a little bit of WOW.
From the outside, it shines like a beacon in Aotea Square. Inside, it’s something else entirely - a sparkling, cosy world where every step surrounds you in soft, golden light.
Subtle by day and radiant after dark, whether you're out for a family night or date night this is a joyful experience not to miss.
Walk it once, snap a pic, tag us @aucklandlive, then go again - you’ll want to!
Hot tip: Visit on a Friday or Saturday night, between 6pm and 9pm, to watch neon-lit dancers bringing an extra touch of magic to the Cathedral. 
Free entry, just turn up and step into the magic. Open 24/7 (best to visit after dark).

title: Ngā Whetū o te Tau Hou | The Stars of the New Year
location: Te Whatu Stardome | Observatory & Planetarium, 670 Manukau Rd, Maungakiekie/One Tree Hill Domain, Epsom, Auckland 1023, Auckland
description:
In this immersive planetarium experience, you’ll journey through the night sky to explore the Matariki star cluster and its importance in Aotearoa and te ao Māori.
Discover the rich pūrākau (stories), science and traditions connected to each of the nine whetū, learn about the Maramataka (the Māori lunar calendar), and reflect on how Matariki guides us through the cycles of the year along with many other significant stars.
Whether you’re reconnecting with Matariki or experiencing it for the first time, this show is a great way to honour the season and gain a deeper appreciation of Māori astronomy and our place within the cosmos.
Keywords: Nga Whetu o te Tau Hou The Stars of the New Year

title: Rethinking Your Job Search Strategy
location: Room 608, WG building, AUT City campus, Auckland
description:
For our next session, we're stepping back from mock interviews to look at the bigger picture: **how to actually approach a job search in today's market.**
We're really excited to host **Cindy Wang**, an Employability and Careers Specialist at AUT, who has kindly agreed to come share her perspective with our community. If you've ever felt like sending out applications into a void, this one's for you.

**About the session**

In today’s competitive job market, sending out countless applications and hoping for the best is no longer an effective job search strategy. This workshop will challenge you to rethink your approach and explore how to strategically position yourself to stand out from other applicants.

You’ll learn how to identify your unique positioning in the job market and effectively communicate your value through your CV and cover letter. The facilitator will also share personal observations about New Zealand workplace culture, along with practical interview tips to help you navigate the local job market with confidence.

Whether you’re looking for your first role in Aotearoa, seeking a career change, or searching for a part-time job, this session will provide actionable strategies and insights to help you approach your job search more intentionally and increase your chances of success.

**About the Facilitator**

Cindy Wang is an Employability and Careers Specialist at AUT. She is passionate about helping people build meaningful and purposeful careers while developing the adaptability needed to thrive in a rapidly changing world of work.

Before joining the Employability and Careers team, Cindy worked as a teaching assistant and workshop facilitator. She holds a Master of Business, specialising in Organisational Psychology, and a Graduate Certificate in Career Development. She is currently working towards her credential as an International Coaching Federation (ICF)-certified coach.

**Who is this for?**
Everyone. Seriously. Whether you're new to New Zealand

* **The event venue entry will be closed at 6:30pm, please make sure you arrive on time.**

**Talk 1: From Zero Interviews to Real Projects: What to Build When No One's Calling Back? by Ismael Silva**
This talk is aimed squarely at where most of the room actually is right now — applying, waiting, wondering if the market has forgotten about them. The core idea is that waiting is the worst use of a junior's time, and there's a better way to spend those weeks that turns a CV into a portfolio and an interview into a conversation about something you've actually built.

The session will show that "building leverage" does not require massive side projects. It will also touch on the value of soft skills and leadership, making the discussion relevant for both junior and experienced developers.

**A bit about Ismael:**

* Ismael is a full-stack engineer specializing in Next.js, TypeScript, Node.js, and Postgres, and currently runs a small product studio called Base Logic Labs. Before transitioning into tech, he spent more than 20 years in public speaking, sales, and leadership roles, delivering over a thousand talks across various settings.

Katrina meets a lot of ambitious young people who seem to believe that it's possible for them to advance in their careers at an aggressive pace (once they get their foot in the door). title: Pacific Dance Festival
location: Auckland
description:
Pacific Dance Festival returns this June with a powerful celebration of contemporary Pacific identity in Aotearoa, bringing together artists from across the Moana in an expanded 2026 programme.
Returning to South Auckland, the cultural heart of the Pacific diaspora, the festival finds home in the Māngere Arts Centre - Ngā Tohu o Uenuku, Te Oro Music and Arts Centre in Glen Innes and Toi Tū - Studio One Toi Tū in Auckland Central.
Festival Director Iosefa Enari MNZM says: “Pacific Dance Festival 2026 is a declaration of who we are now - a diverse, global, future-focused Pacific. Our artists are innovators, storytellers and cultural leaders. This year we honour the full Moana, from Micronesia to Polynesia, and we do it from South Auckland - the home of Pacific creativity.”
The 2026 programme brings together artists from Wallis & Futuna (ʻUvea), Kiribati, Rotuma, Samoa, Aotearoa, and the Indigenous Pacific diaspora of Te Whanganui-a-Tara. The festival spans traditional, contemporary and street-based practice, showcasing established, emerging, and youth voices.
Festival highlights:
CALL TO WALLIS - Justin Haiu 5 - 6 June | Māngere Arts Centre
A powerful contemporary work honouring ʻUvean identity and ancestral memory.
MOANA SHOWCASE 9 June | Māngere Arts Centre
Aotearoa’s leading dance institutions present new Pacific works.
TRIPLE BILL: Kamataga × In the Fale × Vignette of the Frigate 11 June | Māngere Arts Centre
Three contemporary works exploring identity, beginnings, Melanesian womanhood, and Pacific migration.
MAREWEN KIRIBATI YOUTH GROUP - Full Show 2 June | Māngere Arts Centre
A vibrant celebration of Kiribati culture and youth leadership.
SHIFTING CENTRE - THE CIRCLE 15 - 16 June | Māngere Arts Centre
Explosive contemporary dance from Wellington’s Indigenous collective.
SAMOAN LANGUAGE WEEK WORKSHOPS Early June | Toi Tū & Te Oro
Community movement workshops celebrating Gagana Samoa.

all the forest stands with you traces the entangled relationalities between the human and the more-than-human world.
The exhibition brings together artists whose practices connect to a place where whenua, water, air and ancestral presence are not easily reduced to backdrop or resource, but remain active participants in shared worlds. Taking this condition not as an illustration, but as a proposition: to revisit, reevaluate and reimagine the status quo of our being in a world that is never solely human.
